title: Persist profile fields in direct-password participant provisioning
verify: Direct-password participant creation requires trimmed surname and given name, stores fullName and immutable server-generated registeredAt atomically, and preserves existing role/session authority.
Invalid, duplicate, or failed creation leaves account, credential, and profile state unchanged; no migration, backfill, or legacy-row path is introduced.
The Identity & Access profile query exposes only fullName and registeredAt through the accepted Actor Context Boundary; no consumer reads its tables directly.
evidence_required: statistics-projection.md#participant-profile-metadata RED: direct-password participant creation accepts a missing name, omits or mutates registeredAt, or partially commits profile state; GREEN: isolated creation tests prove mandatory surname/given name, trimmed fullName, immutable server timestamp, atomic failure behavior, and no migration/backfill path; artifact: .tasks/TASK-058-T3-FT-007-W27/ and .protocols/TASK-058-T3-FT-007-W27/.
purpose: Make the Identity & Access direct participant path create the profile data required by scoped statistics.
success_outcome: Every newly created direct-password participant has server-owned fullName and registeredAt without changing authority or session semantics.
anti_goals: Do not add migration, backfill, legacy-account handling, or a fallback name.
Do not let profile fields grant role, center, class, membership, or session authority.
Do not expose account tables to Statistics, routes, or components.
constraints: Identity & Access exclusively owns account and profile persistence; the Admin route remains an adapter.
Surname and given name are mandatory creation input and are normalized into one trimmed fullName; registeredAt is server-generated and immutable.
The accepted target population has no legacy accounts without names; do not implement migration, backfill, or legacy handling.
invariants: Account, password credential, and profile fields commit atomically or none is persisted.
Profile metadata never changes role, membership, assignment, authorization, or session state.
Only the named Identity & Access boundary returns profile fields; raw account persistence never crosses a module boundary.
verification_targets: statistics-projection.md#participant-profile-metadata: isolated direct-password success/failure matrix for required names, server timestamp, immutability, and state-before/state-after.
boundary-map.md#actor-context-boundary: source probe proves the profile projection crosses the accepted server boundary and no route/module reads account tables directly.
access-control.md#binding-and-session-rules: role/session behavior remains unchanged after profile persistence.

stop_conditions: Stop if satisfying the accepted profile contract requires inventing, backfilling, or silently substituting a name for an existing account.
Stop if a consumer requires direct Identity & Access table access or a new owner/boundary beyond the accepted Actor Context Boundary.
